Cream and chalk-white rock built up in thin scalloped layers, knobbly and pitted, with tan and orange stain in the hollows and fine cracks. Flat, even, shadowless overcast light so that no side is brighter than another. The surface fills the whole frame edge to edge at one uniform scale, as a seamless tileable texture. The first reference image is the place this material belongs to: take its colours, its age and its character from there, and nothing of its composition. The second reference image is a real photograph: it is the standard for how a camera records a real surface, with real grain, real micro detail and no painted or stylised look. Output one square image. Photographic, sharp from edge to edge, no depth of field blur, no vignette, no horizon, no sky, no text, no logo, no people, no animals.
why: the pale lip where the floor of the lake stops
